title.en: Democrats express ‘grave concerns’ over secretive ICE deportation flights
title.zh: 民主党人对秘密ICE遣返航班表示“严重关切”

summary.en: Forty House Democrats have expressed “grave concerns” over the Trump administration’s secretive program of deportation flights, demanding the FAA address allegations of immigrant mistreatment and the “urgent need for transparency.”
summary.zh: 四十名众议院民主党人对特朗普政府秘密遣返航班计划表示“严重关切”，要求联邦航空管理局（FAA）处理有关移民遭受虐待的指控，并强调“迫切需要透明度”。

body.en: Exclusive: In a letter 40 lawmakers demand the FAA address allegations of mistreatment of immigrants and the ‘urgent need for transparency’ A group of 40 House Democrats have described “grave concerns” over the Trump administration ’s secretive program of deportation flights and demanded the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) address allegations of mistreatment and inhumane conditions on ICE charter jets. In a letter shared with the Guardian and addressed to the FAA administrator, Bryan Bedford, the lawmakers describe the “urgent need for transparency” over ICE ’s expanded use of commercial airliners to transfer detained immigrants and its “inappropriate and dangerous” efforts to shield these flights from public scrutiny. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：40 名议员在一封信中要求美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 处理有关虐待移民的指控以及“迫切需要透明度”。由 40 名众议院民主党人组成的小组对特朗普政府的秘密驱逐航班计划表示“严重关切”，并要求美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 处理有关 ICE 包机上的虐待和不人道条件的指控。在与《卫报》分享并致美国联邦航空管理局局长布莱恩·贝德福德的一封信中，立法者描述了“迫切需要透明度”，因为 ICE 扩大使用商业客机来转移被拘留的移民，并为保护这些航班免受公众监督而做出的“不恰当且危险的”努力。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for transparency and an end to alleged mistreatment of immigrants echoes a timeless biblical principle: how we treat the foreigner reflects our own humanity. Leviticus 19:33-34 reminds us that those residing among us, even if not native-born, deserve to be treated with love and dignity, remembering our own past vulnerabilities. This principle urges...
reflection.zh: 要求透明并停止对移民的虐待，这与一个永恒的圣经原则不谋而合：我们如何对待寄居者，反映了我们自身的人性。利未记19:33-34提醒我们，居住在我们中间的人，即使不是本地出生，也应得到爱和尊严的对待，并要记住我们自己也曾是寄居者。这一原则敦促我们确保所有人，特别是弱势群体，都能获得公正和怜悯。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Trump says he hopes to achieve ‘a lot’ ahead of China visit, with several CEOs set to join president in Beijing – live
title.zh: 特朗普本周将前往中国会见习近平，伊朗战争和贸易争端笼罩峰会——美国政治直播

summary.en: US President Trump is scheduled to visit China this week for a summit with President Xi, marking the first such visit in nearly a decade. The high-stakes meeting comes amidst significant international tensions, including an ongoing war in Iran and unresolved trade disputes.
summary.zh: 美国总统特朗普本周将前往中国与习近平主席举行峰会，这是近十年来美国总统首次访华。此次高层会晤正值国际紧张局势加剧之际，包括正在进行的伊朗战争和悬而未决的贸易争端。

body.en: Seventeen tech and finance CEOs to join Trump on China trip; it will be the first US presidential visit China since Trump went in 2017 Sign up for the Breaking News US email Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump reiterated that Iran’s peace proposal was “just unacceptable”. The president went on to insist that he had a “very simple plan”, and maintained that Tehran could not have a nuclear weapon, without elaborating on the next negotiating steps. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这将是美国总统近十年来首次访问中国，上一次访问是特朗普在2017年。 特朗普在椭圆形办公室对记者发表讲话时重申，伊朗的和平提议“简直不可接受”。总统接着坚称他有一个“非常简单的计划”，并坚称德黑兰不能拥有核武器，但没有详细说明下一步的谈判步骤。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As leaders gather for crucial talks amidst global tensions, the pursuit of peace remains a constant challenge. Romans 12:18 reminds us of the ongoing call to live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on us. This principle guides diplomatic efforts to navigate complex disputes and seek stability, even when full agreement seems distant.
reflection.zh: 当各国领导人在全球紧张局势中齐聚进行关键会谈时，追求和平仍然是一个持续的挑战。《罗马书》12:18提醒我们，要尽力与众人和睦相处。这一原则指导着外交努力，以应对复杂的争端并寻求稳定，即使完全达成一致似乎遥不可及。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Middle East crisis live: Trump says ceasefire is ‘on massive life support’ after rejecting Iran’s response to US peace proposal
title.zh: 中东危机：特朗普拒绝伊朗对美国和平提议的回应，德黑兰警告将发动新袭击

summary.en: The US president has rejected Iran's response to a peace proposal, calling it “totally unacceptable.” Tehran, in turn, has warned of retaliation against any new US strikes or foreign warships in the Strait of Hormuz, as a ceasefire in the region frays.
summary.zh: 美国总统已拒绝伊朗对和平提议的回应，称其“完全不可接受”。德黑兰则警告称，如果美国再次发动袭击或有外国军舰进入霍尔木兹海峡，伊朗将进行报复，目前该地区的停火协议正在瓦解。

body.en: US president said Iran’s response to the US peace proposal was ‘stupid’ and that the ceasefire is ‘unbelievable weak’ Trump calls Iran’s response to peace plan ‘totally unacceptable’ as ceasefire frays Turkey’s foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, will visit Qatar later today for talks on the war, its impact on the region and efforts to ensure navigational safety in the strait of Hormuz is resumed, a Turkish diplomatic source told the Reuters news agency. Turkey, which neighbours Iran, has been in close contact with the US, Iran and mediator Pakistan since the start of the conflict. It condemnded the US and Israel for launching the war, widely seen to have been done illegally, but also criticised Iran’s counter strikes on Gulf states. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国总统称伊朗的反应“完全不可接受”，而德黑兰则表示将对美国任何新的袭击或外国军舰进入霍尔木兹海峡进行报复。特朗普称伊朗对和平计划的反应“完全不可接受”，因为在美国和以色列于2月28日杀死伊朗前最高领导人后不久，真主党开始向以色列开火。以色列以空袭回应，并对黎巴嫩南部发动地面入侵。以色列军队现在占领了黎巴嫩边境沿线的一小片土地。官员声称他们希望建立一个“安全区”来保护以色列北部社区免受真主党的袭击。但这引发了人们对长期占领的担忧。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rejection of a peace proposal and subsequent threats of retaliation highlight the persistent challenge of breaking cycles of conflict. In such moments, it is easy for nations to be overcome by the temptation to respond to perceived evil with further aggression. Yet, the call remains to seek ways to overcome evil with good, even when peace seems distant.
reflection.zh: 和平提议被拒绝以及随之而来的报复威胁，凸显了打破冲突循环的持续挑战。在这样的时刻，国家很容易被诱惑，以进一步的侵略来回应所认为的邪恶。然而，即使和平看似遥远，我们仍被呼召寻求以善胜恶的途径。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: A messy day for Starmer: is Labour ungovernable? – podcast
title.zh: 斯塔默的混乱一天：工党是否无法治理？——播客

summary.en: Labour leader Keir Starmer faced a challenging day marked by internal dissent, including a speech aimed at deterring leadership challenges, public support for a rival from his deputy, and calls for his resignation from other MPs.
summary.zh: 工党领袖基尔·斯塔默度过了充满挑战的一天，党内异议不断，包括他发表旨在阻止领导权挑战的演讲，其副手公开支持另一位潜在领袖，以及其他议员呼吁他辞职。

body.en: More ways to listen Apple podcasts Spotify RSS Feed Download Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey , produced by Frankie Tobi , music by Axel Kacoutié , the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj Mon 11 May 2026 15.54 EDT Share 00:00:00 00:00:00 Keir Starmer kicked off the day with a speech aimed at persuading MPs against launching any kind of leadership challenge. By lunchtime, Angela Rayner was speaking at the CWU conference calling for Andy Burnham to return. In the afternoon the list of MPs calling on him to resign was slowly creeping up but no challenge has materialised. Why is the Labour party in such a muddle over Starmer?
body.zh: 更多收听 Apple 播客的方式 Spotify RSS Feed 下载 由 Pippa Crerar 和 Kiran Stacey 主持，Frankie Tobi 制作，Axel Kacoutié 音乐，执行制作人 Maz Ebtehaj Mon 11 五月 2026 15.54 EDT 分享 00:00:00 00:00:00 Keir Starmer 以旨在说服的演讲拉开了当天的序幕议员们反对发起任何形式的领导力挑战。午餐时间，安吉拉·雷纳 (Angela Rayner) 在 CWU 会议上发表讲话，呼吁安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 回归。下午，要求他辞职的议员名单慢慢增加，但没有任何挑战成为现实。为什么工党在斯塔默问题上如此混乱？

reflection.en: The internal challenges faced by political leaders often highlight the tension between individual ambition and collective purpose. Philippians 2:3 reminds us that true strength in leadership, and indeed in any community, comes from humility and valuing others above oneself. When personal aspirations overshadow shared goals, unity can quickly unravel,...
reflection.zh: 政治领袖所面临的内部挑战，常凸显个人抱负与集体目标之间的张力。腓立比书2:3提醒我们，领导力乃至任何群体真正的力量，都源于谦卑并将他人看得比自己更重要。当个人抱负盖过共同目标时，团结便会迅速瓦解，导致混乱。

verse.textEn: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.
verse.textZh: 凡事不可结党，不可贪图虚浮的荣耀；只要存心谦卑，各人看别人比自己强。

title.en: Four ministerial aides quit and more than 60 MPs call for Keir Starmer’s resignation as speech fails to quell rebellion – UK politics live
title.zh: 基尔·斯塔默誓言“证明怀疑者是错的”，以避免领导权挑战——英国政治直播

summary.en: Keir Starmer, leader of the Labour Party, is attempting to overcome a leadership challenge by making significant policy promises, including nationalizing British Steel and improving relations with Europe. This comes as many voters express a feeling that the country is not working for them.
summary.zh: 工党领袖基尔·斯塔默正试图通过提出重要的政策承诺来避免领导权挑战，其中包括将英国钢铁国有化并重建与欧洲的关系。在此之际，许多选民表示感觉国家未能为他们服务。

body.en: Labour MPs say prime minister did not ‘did not speak clearly enough’ this morning and urged him to set a timetable for his exit Botterill says voters she spoke to during the campaign felt the country does not work for them. She is a working-class Yorkshire woman, she says. She knows that the opportunities she has enjoyed would not be there if if had not been for the achievements of Labour government. She says Labour is one of the best vehicles for changing the lives of working people that this county has ever known. Continue reading...
body.zh: 英国首相在他的成败演说中承诺将英国钢铁公司国有化，并重建与欧洲的关系。博特里尔表示，她在竞选期间与选民交谈的选民认为，这个国家不适合他们。她说，她是约克郡的工人阶级女性。她知道，如果没有工党政府所取得的成就，她所享有的机会就不会存在。她说，工党是该县有史以来改变劳动人民生活的最佳工具之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In times when people feel their nation lacks direction, leaders often step forward to articulate a new vision. Proverbs 29:18 reminds us that without a clear vision, people can become disoriented and lose their way. This highlights the profound responsibility of leadership to offer hope and a path forward, addressing the deep-seated concerns of the populace.
reflection.zh: 当人们感到国家缺乏方向时，领袖们常会站出来阐明新的愿景。箴言29:18提醒我们，没有清晰的异象，百姓就会放纵，失去方向。这突显了领导者提供希望和前进道路的深远责任，以回应民众深层的担忧。

verse.textEn: Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint; but blessed is the one who heeds wisdom's instruction.
verse.textZh: 没有异象，民就放肆；惟遵守律法的，便为有福。

title.en: Could Delta Goodrem be a winner? Everything you need to know about Eurovision 2026
title.zh: 黛尔塔·古德莱姆会是赢家吗？关于2026年欧洲歌唱大赛你需要知道的一切

summary.en: The 70th Eurovision Song Contest is approaching, with speculation rising about potential winners like Delta Goodrem. The article provides details on how to watch and what to know about the upcoming international music competition.
summary.zh: 第70届欧洲歌唱大赛即将举行，关于黛尔塔·古德莱姆等潜在获胜者的猜测日益增多。文章提供了关于如何观看以及了解这项国际音乐比赛的详细信息。

body.en:
Sydney-born Delta Goodrem is Australia's pick for the 70th Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna, Austria. Source: Getty / Christian Bruna

Bust out your sequins, set your alarms: it's Eurovision time again, and this year, some say Australia has good odds.

Thirty-five nations will battle it out across a week in Vienna, Austria, for the 70th anniversary of the Eurovision Song Contest.

This year marks 11 years since Australia joined the competition in 2015 with a wildcard invitation.

Award-winning singer-songwriter Delta Goodrem is representing Australia with her song Eclipse in Eurovision 2026.

Goodrem could be the key to victory, according to Jess Carniel, a Eurovision researcher and associate professor at the University of Southern Queensland.

"She's a very experienced professional, polished performer who can really pull off a big show like this," she said.

Carniel said Goodrem's already established European fan base will help Australia go the distance in the contest.

"She's done tours there, and she has cultivated a European audience who are really looking forward to seeing her perform.

"Looking at the betting odds ... we're currently sitting fifth — that's huge. This is before the contest, before any of the semi-finals or before any of us have seen these performances."

Broadcast to a global audience of 166 million, Eurovision continues to cement its place as the world's most popular singing contest.

"The audience in Australia definitely grew when we started participating; some of that really is just out of the competitive nature of Australians," she said.

The Eurovision Song Contest started in 1956 with seven competing countries performing two songs each.

"We often say it started to unite war-torn Europe, but really it was for the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) to generate more traction for its new Eurovision television and radio network ... and encourage collaboration and transnational participation."

"People were watching it all over Europe, and it became something that was useful and interesting for broadcasters to sign up to ... it was an international event that had gained a fairly significant national audience, especially for those countries actually competing."

"That's a huge part of what attracts many countries to keep on participating in Eurovision, even when things may be going badly for them in their country, showcasing themselves on a global stage has been really, really important."

Eurovision received a massive boost in the late 90s and early 2000s, after the dissolution of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR).

"All these new countries, it was important for them to show themselves as these newly independent states — to be able to show their culture, their language, as distinct from that...
body.zh: 出生于悉尼的 Delta Goodrem 被澳大利亚选拔参加在奥地利维也纳举行的第 70 届欧洲歌唱大赛。资料来源：盖蒂/克里斯蒂安·布鲁纳 拿出你的亮片，设置好闹钟：又到了欧洲电视网的时间，而今年，有人说澳大利亚有很好的胜算。 35 个国家将在奥地利维也纳进行为期一周的角逐，庆祝欧洲歌唱大赛 70 周年。 自2015年澳大利亚以外卡邀请参加比赛以来，今年已经11周年了。 屡获殊荣的创作型歌手 Delta Goodrem 将代表澳大利亚凭借歌曲《Eclipse》参加 2026 年欧洲歌唱大赛。 欧洲电视网研究员、南昆士兰大学副教授杰西·卡尼尔表示，古德雷姆可能是获胜的关键。 她说：“她是一位经验丰富、专业、出色的表演者，真正能够完成这样的大型演出。” 卡尼尔表示，古德雷姆已经建立的欧洲粉丝基础将帮助澳大利亚在比赛中走得更远。 “她在那里进行了巡演，并培养了一批非常期待看到她表演的欧洲观众。 “看看投注赔率……我们目前排名第五——这是巨大的。这是在比赛之前，在任何半决赛之前，或者在我们任何人看到这些表演之前。” 欧洲歌唱大赛向全球 1.66 亿观众播出，继续巩固其作为世界上最受欢迎的歌唱比赛的地位。 “当我们开始参与时，澳大利亚的观众肯定有所增加；其中一些确实只是出于澳大利亚人的竞争本性，”她说。 欧洲歌唱大赛始于 1956 年，七个参赛国家各表演两首歌曲。 “我们经常说它开始团结饱受战争蹂躏的欧洲，但实际上是欧洲广播联盟（EBU）为其新的欧洲电视网和广播网络产生更多吸引力……并鼓励合作和跨国参与。” “整个欧洲的人们都在观看这一赛事，对于广播公司来说，报名参加这项赛事既有用又有趣……这是一项国际赛事，赢得了相当多的全国观众，特别是对于那些真正参赛的国家来说。” “这是吸引许多国家继续参加欧洲歌唱大赛的一个重要原因，即使他们的国家的情况可能很糟糕，但在全球舞台上展示自己确实非常重要。” 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟 (苏联) 解体后，欧洲歌唱大赛在 90 年代末和 2000 年代初得到了巨大的发展。 “所有这些新国家，对他们来说，重要的是要展示自己是这些新独立的国家——能够展示他们的文化、他们的语言，与其他国家不同......

reflection.en: The excitement around Eurovision highlights the human drive to compete and achieve recognition. While the pursuit of excellence and a coveted prize can be motivating, this verse reminds us that earthly crowns are perishable. It invites us to consider what we strive for with lasting discipline, seeking a reward that endures beyond fleeting fame.
reflection.zh: 欧洲歌唱大赛的激动人心之处，凸显了人类竞争并获得认可的动力。虽然追求卓越和梦寐以求的奖项可以激励人心，但这节经文提醒我们，地上的冠冕是会朽坏的。它邀请我们思考，我们以持久的自律所追求的是什么，寻求那超越短暂名声、永恒的奖赏。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Portrait looted by Nazis found in home of Dutch SS leader's descendants
title.zh: 纳粹掠夺的肖像画在荷兰党卫军领导人后代家中被发现

summary.en: A portrait believed to have been plundered by high-ranking Nazi Hermann Goering during World War Two has been found in the home of descendants of a Dutch SS leader.
summary.zh: 一幅据信在二战期间被纳粹高级官员赫尔曼·戈林掠夺的肖像画，在一名荷兰党卫军领导人的后代家中被发现。

body.en:
A painting stolen by Nazis from a Jewish art collector in the Netherlands during World War Two has been found in the home of descendants of a notorious Dutch SS collaborator, an art detective says.

Portrait of a Young Girl, by Dutch artist Toon Kelder, is believed to have hung for decades in the home of Hendrik Seyffardt's family, Arthur Brand said. He added later it had been handed over to his team.

The painting belonged to Jacques Goudstikker, who died fleeing the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands, leaving a collection of more than 1,000 paintings.

The case was brought to Brand's attention by a man who told him he was a descendant of Seyffardt "disgusted" to learn his family had kept the artwork for years.

Seyffardt was a Dutch general who commanded a Waffen-SS unit of volunteers on the eastern front before he was assassinated by resistance fighters in 1943.

Shortly after learning he was related to the Nazi collaborator, the man approached his grandmother to ask about the painting's history.

She is said to have told him it had been purchased during World War Two and that it was "Jewish looted art, stolen from Goudstikker. It is unsellable. Don't tell anyone."

The family, which changed their name at the end of the war, have admitted being in possession of the painting but denied knowing its true origin, according to a statement to Dutch media.

After learning of the painting's history, the family member contacted Brand through an intermediary, believing the only way for it to be returned was for the story to be made public.

The family member told Dutch outlet De Telegraaf: "I feel ashamed. The painting should be returned to the heirs of Goudstikker."

In a statement to the same newspaper, his grandmother said: "I received it from my mother.

"Now that you confront me like this, I understand that Goudstikker's heirs want the painting back. I didn't know that."

Upon being informed of the painting's existence, Brand launched his own investigation.

He discovered the painting had a label on the back and the number 92 etched into its frame.

Brand then searched the archives of a 1940 auction where much of Goudstikker's looted collection was sold and discovered an item under the number 92 titled "Portrait of a Young Girl" by Toon Kelder.

Brand believes the painting had been plundered by Hermann Goering, one of the most powerful figures in the Nazi Party, when Goudstikker fled for Britain in 1940.

It was then sold to Seyffardt at auction before being handed down to his descendant, Brand says.

After launching his investigation, Brand contacted the lawyers of Goudstikker's heirs, who he said confirmed the collector had previously owned six paintings by Toon Kelder.

body.zh: 一名艺术侦探称，在一名臭名昭著的荷兰党卫军合作者的后裔家中，发现了第二次世界大战期间纳粹从一名犹太艺术收藏家手中偷走的一幅画。 阿瑟·布兰德 (Arthur Brand) 表示，荷兰艺术家 Toon Kelder 创作的《年轻女孩的肖像》据信在亨德里克·塞法特 (Hendrik Seyffardt) 的家里挂了几十年。他后来补充说，该项目已移交给他的团队。 这幅画属于一位犹太艺术品经销商，他在逃离纳粹入侵荷兰时丧生，留下了 1000 多幅画作的收藏。 一名男子引起了布兰德的注意，他告诉布兰德，他是塞法特的后裔，当得知他的家人多年来一直保留这件艺术品时，他“感到厌恶”。 塞法特是一位荷兰将军，在 1943 年被抵抗战士暗杀之前，曾在东线指挥一支由武装党卫队志愿者组成的部队。 在得知自己与纳粹合作者有关系后不久，该男子找到他的祖母询问这幅画的历史。 据说她告诉他，这件作品是在第二次世界大战期间购买的，是“犹太人从艺术品经销商雅克·古德斯蒂克（Jacques Goudstikker）那里偷来的艺术品。它无法出售。不要告诉任何人。” 根据荷兰媒体的一份声明，这个在战争结束时改名的家族承认拥有这幅画，但否认知道其真实来源。 在得知这幅画的历史后，布兰德的家人通过中间人联系了布兰德，认为归还这幅画的唯一途径就是将故事公之于众。 这位家庭成员告诉荷兰媒体 De Telegraaf：“我感到羞愧。这幅画应该归还给 Goudstikker 的继承人。” 在同一家报纸的一份声明中，他的祖母说：“我从我母亲那里收到了它。 “既然你这样面对我，我就明白古德斯蒂克的继承人想要拿回这幅画。我不知道这一点。” 在得知这幅画的存在后，布兰德展开了自己的调查。 他发现这幅画的背面有一个标签，画框上刻着数字 92。 随后，布兰德搜查了 1940 年拍卖会的档案，Goudstikker 的大部分被掠夺的藏品都被出售，并在编号 92 下发现了一件由 Toon Kelder 创作的题为“年轻女孩的肖像”的物品。 布兰德认为，1940 年古德斯蒂克逃往英国时，这幅画被纳粹党最有权势的人物之一赫尔曼·戈林 (Hermann Goering) 掠夺。 布兰德说，它随后在拍卖会上卖给了塞法特，然后传给了他的后代。 发起调查后，布兰德联系了古德斯蒂克继承人的律师，他说，后者证实这位收藏家之前曾拥有图恩·凯尔德的六幅画作。 他补充说，律师还向他证实这些画作是……

title.en: Elon Musk and Tim Cook among CEOs expected to accompany Trump on China trip
title.zh: 埃隆·马斯克和蒂姆·库克等首席执行官预计将陪同特朗普中国之行

summary.en: A total of 17 US executives are set to join the president on his visit, where he will meet his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is expected to bring a host of top business and technology industry executives on his trip to China this week.

Among those set to join the president on his official trip to Beijing are Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, Larry Fink of BlackRock, as well as other executives from Meta, Visa, JP Morgan, Boeing, Cargill and more.

In total, 17 US executives will join Trump on the trip, a White House official with knowledge of the plans told the BBC.

The trip is seen as important for the US, as Trump will meet with President Xi Jinping at a time of growing economic and technological animosity between the two countries.

Chuck Robbins, chief executive and chairman of Cisco, had been invited to be a part of the trip "but is unable to due to earnings," according to a company spokeswoman.

Together, the executives represent a swath of US business interests, from social media and consumer hardware, to computer chips and commercial manufacturing.

A spokeswoman for Illumina, a biotechnology company based in Californa, said Thaysen "is honored to be part of the delegation" and that the company hopes the trip will be "an opportunity to strengthen relationships and shape the future of precision medicine."

Representatives of the other companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump's visit to China marks a key test of a fragile trade truce between the two countries, following a tit-for-tat trade war which saw them roll out tariffs which at times topped 100%.

The tariffs were paused in October 2025 after Trump's last meeting with Xi, which took place in South Korea.

Looming large over the upcoming meeting will be the US and Israel's war in Iran , which has already forced a delay to Trump and Xi's meeting.

Trump is expected to push China, which relies on Iran for cheap oil, to help facilitate an agreement between Tehran and Washington to end the war.

China also wants the conflict to end. It has limited the supply of oil to the country, hitting the buying power of other countries around the world that import Chinese goods.

But China's vast oil reserves and diverse energy supply have helped it so far in weathering the fallout of the war better than many neighbours.
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周预计将携带一批商业和科技行业的高级管理人员访问中国。 即将随总统正式访问北京的人士包括苹果公司的蒂姆·库克、特斯拉和 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克、贝莱德的拉里·芬克，以及来自 Meta、Visa、摩根大通、波音、嘉吉等公司的其他高管。 一位了解该计划的白宫官员告诉 BBC，总共有 17 名美国高管将与特朗普一起出访。 这次访问对美国来说非常重要，因为特朗普将在两国经济和技术敌意日益加剧之际会见习近平主席。 思科公司发言人表示，思科首席执行官兼董事长查克·罗宾斯曾受邀参加此次旅行，“但由于盈利原因未能成行”。 这些高管共同代表了美国的一系列商业利益，从社交媒体和消费硬件到计算机芯片和商业制造。 总部位于加利福尼亚州的生物技术公司 Illumina 的发言人表示，塞森“很荣幸成为代表团的一员”，该公司希望这次旅行将成为“加强关系和塑造精准医疗未来的机会”。 其他公司的代表没有立即回应置评请求。 特朗普对中国的访问标志着两国之间脆弱的贸易休战的一次关键考验，此前两国在针锋相对的贸易战中征收了有时高达100%的关税。 特朗普在韩国与习近平最后一次会面后，关税于 2025 年 10 月暂停。 即将举行的会议的一大焦点将是美国和以色列在伊朗的战争，这已经迫使特朗普和习近平的会面推迟。 预计特朗普将推动依赖伊朗获取廉价石油的中国帮助促成德黑兰和华盛顿之间达成协议以结束战争。 中国也希望结束冲突。它限制了该国的石油供应，打击了进口中国商品的世界其他国家的购买力。 但迄今为止，中国丰富的石油储量和多样化的能源供应帮助其比许多邻国更好地抵御了战争的影响。

title.en: Trump says Iran ceasefire is on 'massive life support'

summary.en: The US president criticizes an Iranian counteroffer to end the war, and says the month-long ceasefire is "unbelievably weak".
summary.zh: 美国总统批评了伊朗为结束战争提出的反建议，并表示为期一个月的停火“弱得令人难以置信”。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has said the month-long ceasefire between the US and Iran is on "massive life support".

He told reporters in the Oval Office on Monday that while the ceasefire remained in place, it was "unbelievably weak".

Iran laid out its demands to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz in a counter-offer sent to the US on Sunday. Trump rejected the proposal, calling it "totally unacceptable" and a "piece of garbage".

Esmail Baghaei, a foreign ministry spokesperson for Iran, responded by saying Tehran's proposals were "responsible" and "generous".

Tehran's offer includes an immediate end to the war on all fronts - a reference to the continued Israeli attacks against Iran-supported Hezbollah in Lebanon - a halt to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and guarantees of no further attacks on Iran, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency.

It also reportedly includes a demand for compensation for war damage and an emphasis on Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump criticised the proposal, writing on Truth Social on Sunday: "I have just read the response from Iran's so-called 'Representatives.' I don't like it - TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE."

In response to Trump's comments, Baghaei said Iran would act "in any way necessary to secure our interests".

Speaking in the Oval Office later on Monday, Trump addressed the ceasefire between the two countries which has largely been observed since April despite occasional exchanges of fire.

He told reporters: "I would say the ceasefire is on massive life support... when the doctor walks in and says, 'Sir, your loved one has approximately a 1 percent chance of living'."

The US president said Iran's leaders were "very dishonourable people", adding: "Look, I've had to deal with them four or five times - they change their mind."

"That piece of garbage they sent us - I didn't even finish reading it," he said.

Trump also accused Iran of going back on an agreement to allow the US to remove its supply of enriched uranium. He insisted that Iran would "never have a nuclear weapon".

Iran's Tasnim news agency quoted a source close to the negotiating team as saying: "There is no such thing in Iran's proposal as accepting taking out enriched nuclear material."

But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium must be "taken out" before the war can be considered over.

"There's still enrichment sites that have to be dismantled," Netanyahu said in an interview on CBS's 60 Minutes show.

US news outlet Axios reported that the initial one-page, 14-point US memorandum includes provisions such as a suspension on Iranian nuclear enrichment, the lifting of sanctions, and restoring free transit through the Strait of Hormuz.

title.en: US passengers quarantining in Nebraska as officials say public hantavirus risk 'very low'

body.en:
Eighteen Americans evacuated from a cruise ship after possible exposure to hantavirus are being closely monitored by health officials, as authorities say the risk to the public remains "very, very low".

Officials say one passenger aboard the Dutch vessel MV Hondius has tested positive for the Andes virus - a rare type of hantavirus - while another is showing mild symptoms.

More than 90 passengers of the cruise ship, currently docked in Spain's Canary Islands, are being repatriated.

The positive result marks the first confirmed case involving an American passenger. Two people are being monitored in Atlanta, while 16 others are in Nebraska at the nation's only national quarantine unit.

"No-one who poses a risk to public health is walking out the front door onto the streets of Omaha," Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen said at a press conference alongside health officials on Monday morning.

In an effort to preserve space at the facility in Nebraska, some passengers were flown to Atlanta, including the passenger who displayed mild symptoms, said Brendan Jackson of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The two individuals taken to Georgia include one who is symptomatic and that person's partner.

"Let me be crystal clear: the risk of hantavirus to the general public remains very, very low," said Admiral Brian Christine of the US Health and Human Services department (HHS). "The Andes variant of this virus does not spread easily, and it requires prolonged close contact with someone who is already symptomatic."

Experts say most strains of hantavirus, a group of viruses carried by rodents, do not pass from person to person, but the Andes strain identified in a number of people who had been on the Dutch cruise ship does.

The 16 passengers who were taken to Nebraska are in "good shape" and "good spirits", Michael Wadman, medical director of the National Quarantine Unit, said.

He said the person who had tested positive to Andes virus was placed in a biocontainment facility and was not experiencing any symptoms.

The CDC cautioned that people could have symptoms, but that did not mean that they necessarily had the hantavirus. Any symptoms of a mild cold would count as a symptom, Brendan Jackson of CDC said, noting that they were being extra cautious.

When health officials announced that one individual tested "mildly positive" on a PCR test, it raised questions about that terminology.

That patient's specimen was taken on the ship, not in the US, Jackson said noting that there were two specimens collected from that patient, one of which was positive and the other negative.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及在压力下的忠信与属灵勇气。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Bengal, a region known for its secular traditions, is seeing a rise of religion in politics as Islamists grow stronger on the Bangladesh side of the border and Hindu nationalist BJP takes power in India's West Bengal.

Religious and ethnic divisions are growing deeper in Bengal, a region divided between India and Bangladesh. Politicians on both sides of the border are seeking to capitalize on religious sentiment.

In Bangladesh, the February parliamentary elections marked a major moment for Islamist politics , with Jamaat-e-Islami winning nearly one third of the votes nationwide — its strongest showing yet.

In India's West Bengal, the  Hindu nationalist BJP surged from about 10% vote share in 2016 to nearly 46% this year. Under the state's "first past the post" electoral system, this was enough for the BJP to secure 207 out of 294 seats in the state assembly last month .

Bangladeshi anthropologist Rezwana Karim Snigdha warns of an "ill-motivated" shift in rhetorics in Bengal.

The region once boasted a "shared identity" which "allowed people to be both Bengali and Hindu, or Bengali and Muslim," she told DW. "But on both sides of the border, political narratives are increasingly framing identity in religious terms, sidelining language, culture and heritage."

Bengal, broadly the land of Bengali-speaking people, has been divided several times over the centuries, most notably in 1905 when British rulers under Viceroy Lord Curzon split the Bengal Presidency along religious lines.

At the time, Bengal was the center of anti-colonial resistance, and the partition aimed to break this unity by setting the Hindu-majority west against the Muslim-majority east. London hoped to undermine the growing nationalist movement before it could seriously challenge British rule.

Muslim Bengalis in the east, centered around Dhaka, largely welcomed the 1905 partition as it created a region where they would form a majority. In contrast, many Hindu elites opposed the move, seeing it as a threat to their political influence, economic interests and cultural identity.

Indian historian and postcolonial theorist Dipesh Chakrabarty says the "divide and rule" strategy introduced by the British over a century ago still shapes the region today.

"The Hindu elites failed to grasp the moment," he told DW. "Accepting the partition might have reassured Muslims that they were not being dominated."

Strong opposition forced the British to reverse the 1905 partition in 1911, but the underlying divisions persisted. They resurfaced in 1947, when Bengal was split again — this time permanently — between Hindu-majority India and Muslim-majority then East Pakistan.

body.zh: 孟加拉是一个以其世俗传统而闻名的地区，随着伊斯兰主义者在孟加拉边境一侧日益强大，以及印度民族主义人民党在印度西孟加拉邦掌权，宗教在政治中的崛起。 孟加拉地区的宗教和种族分歧日益加深，该地区分为印度和孟加拉国。边境两侧的政治家都在寻求利用宗教情绪。 在孟加拉国，二月份的议会选举标志着伊斯兰政治的一个重要时刻，伊斯兰大会党赢得了全国近三分之一的选票——这是迄今为止最强劲的表现。 在印度西孟加拉邦，印度教民族主义政党印度人民党的得票率从 2016 年的约 10% 飙升至今年的近 46%。根据该邦的“优先当选”选举制度，这足以让印度人民党在上个月的邦议会294个席位中获得207个席位。 孟加拉国人类学家雷兹瓦纳·卡里姆·斯尼格达警告说，孟加拉的言论出现了“动机不良”的转变。 她告诉德国之声，该地区曾经拥有“共同的身份”，“允许人们既是孟加拉人又是印度教徒，或者是孟加拉人和穆斯林”。 “但在边境两侧，政治叙事越来越多地用宗教术语来塑造身份，将语言、文化和遗产边缘化。” 孟加拉是孟加拉语人民的土地，几个世纪以来曾多次分裂，最引人注目的是 1905 年总督寇松勋爵领导下的英国统治者根据宗教信仰分裂了孟加拉总统职位。 当时，孟加拉是反殖民抵抗的中心，分治的目的是通过让印度教徒占多数的西部与穆斯林占多数的东部对抗来打破这种统一。伦敦希望在民族主义运动严重挑战英国统治之前削弱它。 以达卡为中心的东部孟加拉穆斯林在很大程度上欢迎 1905 年的分治，因为它创造了一个他们将占多数的地区。相比之下，许多印度教精英反对此举，认为这是对其政治影响力、经济利益和文化认同的威胁。 印度历史学家和后殖民理论家迪佩什·查克拉巴蒂 (Dipesh Chakrabarty) 表示，英国一个多世纪前推行的“分而治之”战略至今仍在影响着该地区。 “印度教精英未能抓住时机，”他告诉德国之声。 “接受分治可能会让穆斯林放心，他们没有被统治。” 强烈的反对迫使英国于 1911 年推翻了 1905 年的分治，但潜在的分歧仍然存在。 1947 年，它们再次出现，当时孟加拉再次分裂——这一次是永久性的——划分为印度教徒占多数的印度和当时穆斯林占多数的东巴基斯坦。 孟加拉国于 1947 年建国时原本是巴基斯坦的一部分。几年之内，孟加拉穆斯林开始...

summary.en: Nigeria's rising solar imports signal a search for alternatives to unreliable grid power and high fuel costs. But adoption is being held back by steep upfront prices, limited financing and policy uncertainty.

title.en: What will happen to Iran's nuclear material?
title.zh: 伊朗的核材料将会怎样？

summary.en: Iran is believed to have over 440 kilograms of enriched uranium, which could be turned into weapons-grade nuclear material. Despite Trump's pledge to get the "nuclear dust," Tehran has kept it out of US reach.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Iran is believed to have over 440 kilograms of enriched uranium, which could be turned into weapons-grade nuclear material. Despite Trump's pledge to get the "nuclear dust," Tehran has kept it out of US reach.

Iran's nuclear program has been a source of strife for decades, with some Iranians now associating words like as yellowcake, centrifuges, and enrichment with crisis, instability, and war. The regime's insistence on uranium enrichment has exposed the country to heavy sanctions, and some estimates have put the direct economic damage at around $3.5 trillion (€3 trillion).

Throughout the recent military conflicts and fragile ceasefires between Tehran and Washington, the program has once again taken center stage. The United States  seems particularly focused on Iran's nuclear stockpile — Tehran is believed to have over 440 kilograms (970 pounds) of uranium already enriched to 60%, far above what is necessary for civilian purposes. Theoretically, this material could be enriched further to reach 90% in a relatively short time , making it suitable for use in nuclear weapons.

US President Donald Trump often refers to the material as "nuclear dust" in reference to the June 2025 bombing which he claims "obliterated" Iran's nuclear program.

Trump has repeatedly said the US will take possession of it, but also provided contradictory statements on how this will be done, including claims that the US will be "going in, with Iran, with lots of excavators" to dig it out from under the rubble, presumably after a peace accord is reached. In April, Trump said Iran had agreed to hand over its stockpile, while last week he seemed to indicate that the US will "take a hit" because "we have to make a journey down to Iran to take the nuclear weapon."

Iran has yet to confirm any deal involving the uranium stockpile. Talking to US broadcaster CBS in March, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the material remains under the rubble following last year's attack and that Iran had "no program" and "no plan" to recover the material.

However, Araghchi was also careful not to exclude the possibility of diluting the highly enriched uranium as part of a future deal with the US .

Recent media reports also indicated that Iran was ready to dilute part of its stockpile while transferring the rest to a third country. This weekend, Russian President Vladimir Putin said his country was ready store Iran's enriched uranium.

However, it is still unclear where the material is located and what technical challenges needed to be overcome to access it.

Iran's top three nuclear facilities — Isfahan, Fordow and Natanz — all suffered heavy damage during last year's Operation "Midnight Hammer."

title.en: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer 'not walking away' after local election mauling
title.zh: 英国首相凯尔·斯塔默在地方选举遭受重创后“没有走开”

summary.en: Keir Starmer has said he takes "responsibility" for Labour's poor election performance, but also for putting matters right again. "I know I have my doubters and I know I need to prove them wrong, and I will," he said.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 基尔·斯塔默表示，他对工党糟糕的选举表现负有“责任”，但也对纠正问题负有责任。 “我知道有人怀疑我，我知道我需要证明他们是错的，我会的，”他说。 英国首相基尔·斯塔默周一在伦敦语气好斗，表示在上周全国大选惨败后，他无意辞职。 这是在公众压力下做出的，甚至党内也有一些声音敦促他重新考虑自己的立场。 “上周的选举结果很艰难。非常艰难，”斯塔默说。 “这很痛，也应该很痛。我明白。我感觉到了。我承担责任。但这不仅仅是对结果负责。” 他表示，他还有责任解释英国政府计划如何做得更好，并称该国正面临“危险的时期和危险的对手”。 斯塔默说：“如果我们做不好这一点，我们将走上一条非常黑暗的道路。” “我有责任不走开，不让我们的国家陷入混乱，就像保守党一次又一次所做的那样。混乱将对这个国家造成持久的损害。” 他说他知道有人怀疑他，需要证明他们是错的，并表示他会这样做。 斯塔默发表讲话的几天前，他的工党在英国市政选举以及苏格兰和威尔士的国家议会选举中遭受重创，这两个国家都是工党历史上的中心地带。 工党失去了英格兰各地 1,400 多个议会席位，影响力同时流向了民粹主义右翼的改革英国和民粹主义左翼的绿党。 在威尔士参议院，该党的得票率从36.2%、30个席位下降至11.1%、9个席位，从第一大党跌至远远落后于威尔士民族主义者格莱德·西姆鲁党和改革英国党的第三位。 在北方，工党看到苏格兰民族党重新确立了其在荷里路德议院的主导地位，尽管近年来它自己也遇到了重大困难。改革党在苏格兰赢得了与工党一样多的席位； 绿党、保守党和自由民主党紧随其后。 自2024年大选获胜以来，各种政策大转变、沟通问题以及彼得·曼德尔森被任命为美国大使的旷日持久的丑闻让工党面临压力。 周末，资历相对较低的国会议员、前低级别部长凯瑟琳·韦斯特 (Catherine West) 敦促她的同事在周一之前向斯塔默的领导层发起挑战。韦斯特说，如果他们不这样做，她会考虑自己做。 工党备受瞩目的前副党魁安吉拉·雷纳(Angela Rayner)并没有违背斯塔默的信仰，但周日晚上，她确实发布了一份长长的购物清单，列出了她认为工党取得的成就……

title.en: A fight for survival: How the UK soured on PM Keir Starmer and Labour
title.zh: 一场生存之战：英国民众对首相凯尔·斯塔默和工党失去信心

summary.en: Keir Starmer led the UK Labour Party to a landslide victory in 2024, but his leadership is now facing significant challenges and tests.
summary.zh: 凯尔·斯塔默在2024年带领英国工党取得了压倒性胜利，但他的领导力目前正面临严峻的挑战和考验。

body.en:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer's future was thrown into doubt ⁠after his Labour Party ⁠suffered heavy losses in local elections last week. Source: AAP / Maja Smiejkowska/PA

United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who entered office with a confident majority , is now a leader who looks on the ropes, as he fights internal, and external battles.

Less than two years after Starmer led Labour to one of the largest parliamentary majorities in the UK's modern history, his authority is being tested by local election losses , internal rebellion and a public attitude that has hardened against him.

More than 30 Labour MPs have called for him to quit or set out a timetable for his departure, after the party suffered the worst local election defeats for a governing party in more than three decades.

Across 136 English councils, the weekend's electoral test has exposed the scale of Labour's erosion, with Nigel Farage's Reform UK winning more than 1,450 council seats. The right-wing populist party captured former Labour heartlands including Sunderland and Barnsley, key Conservative territories such as Essex and Suffolk, and made major breakthroughs in Scotland and Wales.

At home, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has publicly backed his UK counterpart, telling ABC radio on Monday: "He is a friend of mine, and I hope that Keir Starmer continues to serve as prime minister of the United Kingdom.

"We've dealt with four prime ministers of Great Britain since I was elected as prime minister, and the revolving door of leaders does not lead to stability."

For Starmer, the question is now no longer how to govern from strength — but how to retain power at all.

Labour's 2024 general election victory was initially hailed as an earthquake in British politics.

After 14 years of Conservative rule, voters delivered a decisive repudiation of a government weakened by the enduring fallout of Brexit, Boris Johnson's "partygate" scandal, Liz Truss' market-shaking mini-budget and years of economic stagnation.

Labour secured 411 seats, gaining 209 from its 2019 total — marking its first national victory in 19 years and returning the centre-left party to power for the first time since Tony Blair.

Meanwhile, the Conservatives, also known as the Tories, collapsed to 121 seats, losing 244 in one of the most catastrophic defeats in modern British electoral history.

Starmer campaigned on promises to expand the economy, lower illegal immigration and reduce waiting lists in the National Health Service, presenting Labour as a disciplined corrective to years of Conservative instability.

But for many Britons, the result was less an ideological embrace of Labour than a punitive rejection of Conservative chaos.

title.en: Australia's isolation plan 'one of the stronger responses' to hantavirus globally, Butler says
title.zh: 巴特勒称，澳大利亚的隔离计划是全球应对汉坦病毒的“更强有力措施之一”

summary.en: Australians evacuated from the MV Hondius will quarantine for weeks in a pandemic-era facility outside Perth.
summary.zh: 从“洪迪厄斯”号邮轮撤离的澳大利亚人将在珀斯郊区的一个疫情专用设施中进行为期数周的隔离。

body.en:
The first passengers from the cruise ship began disembarking on Sunday morning, local time. Source: Getty / Chris McGrath

Health Minister Mark Butler says Australia's plan to isolate passengers from a hantavirus-hit cruise ship in a containment facility outside Perth for three weeks is among the strictest global responses to the rare virus.

Four Australian citizens, one permanent resident and a New Zealand national are expected to depart Tenerife in the Canary Islands on an Australian government-supported charter flight at around 3am Tuesday AEST.

Medical personnel will be on board the WA-bound flight, which will land at an RAF base near Perth, and passengers will then be taken to the Bullsbrook Centre for National Resilience.

The biosecurity facility was built by the federal government in 2022 — one of three pandemic prevention facilities, which each have over 500 beds.

None of the repatriated passengers is displaying hantavirus symptoms. Three passengers on the MV Hondius have died , while five others evacuated earlier have fallen ill.

Butler was questioned on why the passengers will quarantine for three weeks, when the incubation period for the illness is up to 42 days.

"Obviously, we will be monitoring advice about what should happen beyond those three weeks. There is an incubation period of 42 days potentially for this virus, but that incubation or the risk of transmission obviously drops off after the first few weeks.

Butler said Australia was taking a "precautionary approach" and acknowledged the Australia-bound passengers may be at more risk of contamination than others, because of the long flight to Australia from Tenerife on a small plane.

"I do make no apology for the fact that this is one of the stronger responses you'll see around the world.

"Many other countries are putting in place quarantine orders at a centre like this or at a hospital, only for two or three days rather than three weeks."

The Australians will be the final group of passengers to leave the ship. Passengers cannot disembark until their plane arrives, and Australia’s flight is scheduled to land last.

Other passengers began disembarking on Sunday morning local time, with several countries having sent planes to repatriate their citizens.

Passengers and port workers at Granadilla in Tenerife wore protective gear during the evacuation, including hazmat suits, face masks and respirators.

Spanish citizens were the first to leave the ship before being flown to Madrid and transferred to a military hospital.

Nearly 150 people were on board when the ship — which was on an Antarctic voyage from South America — arrived in the Spanish territory off the coast of north-west Africa, with all passengers and some crew set to be evacuated.

title.en: Trump rejects Iran's peace proposal response as more drone attacks hit Gulf region
title.zh: 特朗普拒绝伊朗和平提议，更多无人机袭击海湾地区

summary.en: Former President Trump rejected Iran's response to a peace proposal, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated concerns about Iran's nuclear material amidst ongoing drone attacks in the Gulf region.
summary.zh: 前总统特朗普拒绝了伊朗对和平提议的回应，而以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡重申了对伊朗核材料的担忧，同时海湾地区持续发生无人机袭击。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal response via social media. Source: AAP / Jen Golbeck / Sha Dati / Sipa USA

US President Donald Trump branded Iran's terms for ending the Middle East war "totally unacceptable" on Monday, raising the likelihood of renewed conflict after weeks of negotiations.

Iran had responded to the US' latest peace proposal earlier in the day, while warning it would not hold back from retaliating against any new US strikes or permit more foreign warships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump himself provided no details on Iran's counterproposal, but in a brief post on his Truth Social platform made clear he was rejecting it.

"I have just read the response from Iran's so-called 'Representatives.' I don't like it — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!" Trump said.

The back and forth came as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — whose forces launched the war on Iran along with the US military on 28 February — insisted the conflict was not over until Iran's enriched uranium was removed and its nuclear facilities dismantled.

But Iran publicly maintained its defiant line, despite the behind-the-scenes diplomacy.

"We will never bow down to the enemy, and if there is talk of dialogue or negotiation, it does not mean surrender or retreat," Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said via X on Monday.

According to state broadcaster IRIB, Iran's response to the US plan, passed to Pakistani mediators, focuses on ending the war "on all fronts, especially Lebanon" — where Israel has kept up its fight with Iran-backed Hezbollah — as well as on "ensuring shipping security".

It offered little in the way of detail, though the US proposal had reportedly focused on extending the truce in the Gulf to allow for talks on a final settlement of the conflict and on Iran's contested nuclear program.

The impasse unnerved global energy markets, with oil prices opening sharply higher Monday. The international benchmark Brent crude jumped 2.69 per cent to US$104.01 ($144) a barrel on July delivery.

Netanyahu said on Monday that Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium must be removed before the US-Israeli war against Iran could be considered finished.

"It's not over, because there's still nuclear material — enriched uranium — that has to be taken out of Iran. There's still enrichment sites that have to be dismantled," Netanyahu told CBS's "60 Minutes".

He added that Trump was on the same page about the enriched uranium, though the president said in a recent interview that the US could remove it "whenever we want," and that it was "very well surveilled" where it is now.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普通过社交媒体拒绝了伊朗的和平提议。资料来源：AAP / Jen Golbeck / Sha Dati / Sipa 美国 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一称伊朗结束中东战争的条件“完全不可接受”，这增加了经过数周谈判后重新爆发冲突的可能性。 伊朗当天早些时候对美国最新的和平提议做出了回应，同时警告称，它将毫不犹豫地对美国的任何新的袭击进行报复，也不会允许更多的外国军舰进入霍尔木兹海峡。 特朗普本人没有提供有关伊朗反提案的细节，但在他的“真相社交”平台上发表的简短帖子中明确表示他拒绝该提案。 “我刚刚读到了伊朗所谓‘代表’的回应。我不喜欢这样——完全不能接受！”特朗普说道。 以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡（其军队于2月28日与美军一起对伊朗发动了战争）坚称，在伊朗的浓缩铀被运走并拆除其核设施之前，冲突不会结束。 但尽管有幕后外交，伊朗仍公开维持其挑衅路线。 伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安周一通过X表示：“我们永远不会向敌人低头，如果谈论对话或谈判，并不意味着投降或撤退。” 据伊朗国家广播公司IRIB报道，伊朗对美国计划的回应已转交给巴基斯坦调解人，重点是结束“各条战线，特别是黎巴嫩”的战争——以色列一直在黎巴嫩继续与伊朗支持的真主党作战——以及“确保航运安全”。 尽管据报道美国的提议重点是延长海湾地区的停战协议，以便就冲突的最终解决方案和伊朗有争议的核计划进行谈判，但它没有提供太多细节。 这一僵局令全球能源市场感到不安，周一油价大幅高开。 7 月份交割的国际基准布伦特原油价格上涨 2.69%，至每桶 104.01 美元（144 美元）。 内塔尼亚胡周一表示，在美以对伊朗的战争结束之前，必须清除伊朗的浓缩铀库存。 “事情还没有结束，因为仍然有核材料——浓缩铀——必须从伊朗运出。仍然有浓缩设施需要拆除，”内塔尼亚胡告诉哥伦比亚广播公司的“60分钟”节目。 他补充说，特朗普在浓缩铀问题上的看法是一致的，尽管总统在最近的一次采访中表示，美国可以“只要我们想要”就将其移除，而且它现在所在的位置“受到了很好的监视”。 预计特朗普将在访问伊朗时向中国国家主席习近平（伊朗石油的主要买家）施压。

title.en: 'Not another COVID': WHO urges calm ahead of evacuation of hantavirus-hit cruise ship
title.zh: “不要再来一个新冠”：世卫组织敦促保持冷静，准备撤离汉坦病毒感染的邮轮

summary.en: Authorities in the Canary Islands are preparing to evacuate a cruise ship after a hantavirus outbreak killed three passengers.
summary.zh: 加那利群岛当局正准备撤离一艘邮轮，此前船上爆发汉坦病毒，已导致三名乘客死亡。

body.en:
World Health Organization chief Dr Tedros Adhanom said the outbreak was "not another COVID". Source: Getty / Chris McGrath

Countries have prepared to evacuate their citizens from a luxury cruise ship hit by a deadly strain of hantavirus that is due to anchor near the Canary Islands, as health authorities said the risk of the virus spreading was low.

The World Health Organization (WHO) briefed member states with nationals on board on Saturday on how to manage the process , advising active monitoring of passengers for 42 days from the last point of exposure.

"I need you to hear me clearly: this is not another COVID. The current public health risk from hantavirus remains low," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus wrote in a letter to the public published on X earlier.

He said he wanted to take the unusual step of sharing a statement to address people's concerns.

"Passengers will be ferried ashore at the industrial port of Granadilla, far from residential areas, in sealed, guarded vehicles, through a completely cordoned-off corridor, and repatriated directly to their home countries. You will not encounter them," he added.

The luxury cruise ship MV Hondius left for Spain on Wednesday from the coast of Cape Verde off the west coast of Africa after the WHO and European Union asked the country to manage the evacuation of passengers onboard after the hantavirus, which typically begins with flu-like symptoms, was detected.

Usually, the virus is spread by rodents but can in rare cases be transmitted person-to-person.

The WHO on Friday said that eight people had fallen ill, including three who died — a Dutch couple and a German national.

Six of these people are confirmed to have contracted the virus, with another two suspected cases, the WHO has said.

The ship is expected to anchor near the island early Sunday morning, local time.

Local authorities have said the evacuation must take place between midday Sunday midday and around the same time Monday before conditions at sea are expected to become stormier for the rest of the month.

Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, and the Netherlands will send planes to evacuate their citizens aboard the Tenerife-bound cruise ship, Spain's interior minister said in Madrid on Saturday.

The European Union is sending two further planes for the remaining European citizens, Fernando Grande-Marlaska added. The US and UK have confirmed planes and contingency plans were being arranged for non-EU citizens whose countries were unable to send air transport, he said.

British passengers and staff on the cruise ship will be taken to a hospital in northwest England for an initial isolation period once they are repatriated, UK health authorities said on Saturday.

title.en: Elon Musk and Tim Cook among CEOs expected to accompany Trump on China trip
title.zh: 埃隆·马斯克和蒂姆·库克等首席执行官预计将陪同特朗普中国之行

summary.en: A total of 17 US executives are set to join the president on his visit, where he will meet his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is expected to bring a host of top business and technology industry executives on his trip to China this week.

Among those set to join the president on his official trip to Beijing are Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, Larry Fink of BlackRock, as well as other executives from Meta, Visa, JP Morgan, Boeing, Cargill and more.

In total, 17 US executives will join Trump on the trip, a White House official with knowledge of the plans told the BBC.

The trip is seen as important for the US, as Trump will meet with President Xi Jinping at a time of growing economic and technological animosity between the two countries.

Chuck Robbins, chief executive and chairman of Cisco, had been invited to be a part of the trip "but is unable to due to earnings," according to a company spokeswoman.

Together, the executives represent a swath of US business interests, from social media and consumer hardware, to computer chips and commercial manufacturing.

A spokeswoman for Illumina, a biotechnology company based in Californa, said Thaysen "is honored to be part of the delegation" and that the company hopes the trip will be "an opportunity to strengthen relationships and shape the future of precision medicine."

Representatives of the other companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump's visit to China marks a key test of a fragile trade truce between the two countries, following a tit-for-tat trade war which saw them roll out tariffs which at times topped 100%.

The tariffs were paused in October 2025 after Trump's last meeting with Xi, which took place in South Korea.

Looming large over the upcoming meeting will be the US and Israel's war in Iran , which has already forced a delay to Trump and Xi's meeting.

Trump is expected to push China, which relies on Iran for cheap oil, to help facilitate an agreement between Tehran and Washington to end the war.

China also wants the conflict to end. It has limited the supply of oil to the country, hitting the buying power of other countries around the world that import Chinese goods.

But China's vast oil reserves and diverse energy supply have helped it so far in weathering the fallout of the war better than many neighbours.
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周预计将携带一批商业和科技行业的高级管理人员访问中国。 即将随总统正式访问北京的人士包括苹果公司的蒂姆·库克、特斯拉和 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克、贝莱德的拉里·芬克，以及来自 Meta、Visa、摩根大通、波音、嘉吉等公司的其他高管。 一位了解该计划的白宫官员告诉 BBC，总共有 17 名美国高管将与特朗普一起出访。 这次访问对美国来说非常重要，因为特朗普将在两国经济和技术敌意日益加剧之际会见习近平主席。 思科公司发言人表示，思科首席执行官兼董事长查克·罗宾斯曾受邀参加此次旅行，“但由于盈利原因未能成行”。 这些高管共同代表了美国的一系列商业利益，从社交媒体和消费硬件到计算机芯片和商业制造。 总部位于加利福尼亚州的生物技术公司 Illumina 的发言人表示，塞森“很荣幸成为代表团的一员”，该公司希望这次旅行将成为“加强关系和塑造精准医疗未来的机会”。 其他公司的代表没有立即回应置评请求。 特朗普对中国的访问标志着两国之间脆弱的贸易休战的一次关键考验，此前两国在针锋相对的贸易战中征收了有时高达100%的关税。 特朗普在韩国与习近平最后一次会面后，关税于 2025 年 10 月暂停。 即将举行的会议的一大焦点将是美国和以色列在伊朗的战争，这已经迫使特朗普和习近平的会面推迟。 预计特朗普将推动依赖伊朗获取廉价石油的中国帮助促成德黑兰和华盛顿之间达成协议以结束战争。 中国也希望结束冲突。它限制了该国的石油供应，打击了进口中国商品的世界其他国家的购买力。 但迄今为止，中国丰富的石油储量和多样化的能源供应帮助其比许多邻国更好地抵御了战争的影响。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Trump's China visit set to test fragile truce
title.zh: 特朗普访华将考验脆弱的关税休战协议

summary.en: The first US presidential visit to China in almost 10 years will test a fragile tariff truce.
summary.zh: 近十年来首次美国总统访华，将考验一项脆弱的关税休战协议。

body.en:
Beijing has confirmed that US President Donald Trump will travel to China this week to meet Xi Jinping.

The visit, from 13-15 May, will be the first to China by a US president in nearly a decade - and comes at a pivotal moment for ties between the world's two largest economies.

Executives from some of America's biggest companies - including Boeing, Citigroup and Qualcomm - are expected to travel with Trump, potentially to make deals with Chinese firms. It will also mark a key test in the fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing.

In April 2025, Trump unveiled sweeping import taxes on countries across the world, friend or foe.

A major effect of that policy was a tit-for-tat trade war between the US and China that saw them hit each other with tariffs that topped 100%. The tariffs were paused after Trump and Xi's last face-to-face meeting in South Korea in October. But threats from both sides have continued.

Trump won the 2016 election vowing to make trade fairer for the US and to bring manufacturing jobs back to the country.

In 2018, he announced tariffs on $250bn (£185bn) of Chinese imports - the moment that many analysts say the trade war started .

The same year, Trump imposed levies on other trading partners - including Mexico, Canada and Europe - which he said were also taking advantage of the US.

The sweeping measures were a shock, especially for China, said policy researcher Ning Leng from Georgetown University.

"It was the first time they dealt with Trump seriously, and they probably did not expect him to go ahead with it," Leng said.

The US was a key importer of Chinese manufactured goods, putting its workers at risk if American buyers turned away due to Trump's tariffs.

The tensions added to existing issues that have weighed on China's economy for years, including sluggish domestic consumption, high unemployment and a prolonged property crisis.

Exports to the US offered a lifeline for Chinese jobs, but with Trump, that was now put at risk.

"It's harder for one country to withstand a trade war with another that it has a trade surplus with," Leng said.

His administration chose not to lift Trump's tariffs on China, sharing a belief that the US needed to keep a lid on its rival's growth in sectors like technology, Leng said.

Biden also introduced restrictions on Chinese firms, including tech giant Huawei, which was essentially ousted from the US over national security concerns. He also put TikTok under scrutiny, with its US operation eventually being separated from its Chinese parent company.

Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) were also effectively blocked from the US market after heavy tariffs were imposed by Biden.

title.en: Europe should behave more like China does if it wants to survive this age of chaos

summary.en: An article suggests that Europe should abandon its traditional rules and adopt a more pragmatic, assertive approach, similar to China's, to navigate the current global chaos. It argues that while the US and Israel may have initiated the conflict in Iran, Europe and China stand to lose the most.
summary.zh: 一篇文章建议，欧洲若想在当前的全球混乱中生存，就应放弃其传统规则，采取一种更务实、更强硬的做法，类似于中国的行事方式。文章认为，尽管美国和以色列可能挑起了伊朗的冲突，但除了交战方本身，欧洲和中国将是损失最大的。

body.en: Instead of obsessing over rules that have ceased to matter, we must consider giving Beijing a dose of its own medicine The US and Israel may have started the war in Iran, but – apart from the belligerents themselves – it is China and Europe that stand to lose the most from it. Yet while European leaders watch like rabbits caught in the headlights as energy prices shoot through the roof, China has responded to the crisis with remarkable equanimity. It is striking how self-confident Beijing is ahead of this week’s Trump-Xi summit. That’s because China is better prepared for what I call an age of “un-order”. This is not the same as disorder, where rules exist but are broken. Un-order is a world where the rules themselves have simply ceased to matter. While European governments have been obsessed with preserving order, China has been working out how to survive chaos. Mark Leonard is director of the European Council on Foreign Relations and author of Surviving Chaos: Geopolitics When the Rules Fail Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们不应沉迷于已经不再重要的规则，而必须考虑给北京一剂自己的药。美国和以色列可能挑起了伊朗战争，但除了交战双方本身之外，中国和欧洲将是这场战争中损失最大的。然而，当欧洲领导人像被车灯照到的兔子一样眼睁睁地看着能源价格飞涨时，中国却以惊人的冷静应对这场危机。令人惊讶的是，北京在本周的特习峰会之前表现得如此自信。这是因为中国为我所说的“无序”时代做好了更充分的准备。这与无序不同，无序是规则存在但被打破的情况。无秩序是一个规则本身不再重要的世界。当欧洲各国政府一直致力于维护秩序时，中国却一直在研究如何在混乱中生存。马克·伦纳德是欧洲外交关系委员会主任，也是《生存混乱：规则失效时的地缘政治》一书的作者继续阅读...

Yet, the wisdom of Scripture reminds us not to be overcome by evil, but to overcome evil with good. This calls for a steadfast commitment to ethical conduct, even when faced with the allure of pragmatic but morally compromising...

title.en: The geopolitical weaponization of shipping channels
title.zh: 航运渠道的地缘政治武器化

summary.en: The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has renewed focus on other key shipping routes. Experts warn that waterways like the Taiwan Strait or the Strait of Malacca are increasingly used to exert pressure.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has renewed focus on other key shipping routes. Experts warn that waterways like the Taiwan Strait or the Strait of Malacca are increasingly used to exert pressure.

Could imposing a toll to pass through the Strait of Malacca, the narrow stretch of water that connects the Indian Ocean with the Pacific, be a profitable business?

Indonesia's Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa seemed to float the idea at the end of April. "If we split it three ways between Indonesia , Malaysia, and Singapore, that could be quite something, right?" he said.

He later clarified that he was not being entirely serious after Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono said that his country supported the freedom of navigation and would not be imposing tolls on vessels passing through the strait, which runs between Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.

Nonetheless, the remark raised the specter of maritime traffic being misused for geopolitical leverage, not just in the Strait of Hormuz , but in other waterways, too. "The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has forced policymakers in Asia to face questions over the security of other maritime chokepoints," wrote the Reuters news agency.

The Strait of Malacca is of particular concern. This is the most important  shipping route between East Asia, the Middle East, and Europe, accounting for around 22% of international maritime trade.

But there are other issues of concern besides piracy and regional conflict. In November last year, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) warned of this new danger.

Even non-state actors are now in a position to seriously disrupt the flow of global trade, the think tank said, citing attacks by the Houthi militia in the Red Sea. Many shipping companies now avoid passing through the Suez Canal, taking the longer route around the Cape of Good Hope instead, which significantly impacts supply chains and prices.

Political scientist Nikolaus Scholik, former colonel in the Austrian army and senior advisor at the Austria Institute for European and Security Policy (AIES), believes that these are signs of a fundamental change in the geopolitical balance of power .

"We are experiencing today the consequences of a development in which individual states believe they can legally dominate strategically important maritime straits," he told DW. It would be particularly dangerous, he added, if straits like Hormuz, Malacca, or Taiwan were to become levers of geopolitical influence.

body.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡周围的危机重新引起人们对其他主要航线的关注。专家警告说，台湾海峡或马六甲海峡等水道越来越多地被用来施加压力。 对穿过马六甲海峡（连接印度洋与太平洋的狭窄水域）征收通行费是否是一项有利可图的生意？ 印度尼西亚财政部长普尔巴亚·尤迪·萨德瓦 (Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa) 似乎在四月底提出了这个想法。 “如果我们将其分成印度尼西亚、马来西亚和新加坡三部分，那可能会很了不起，对吧？”他说。 他后来澄清说，在印度尼西亚外交部长苏吉奥诺表示印度尼西亚支持航行自由并且不会对通过印度尼西亚、马来西亚和新加坡之间的海峡的船只征收通行费后，他并不是完全认真的。 尽管如此，这一言论引发了人们对海上交通被滥用于地缘政治影响力的担忧，不仅在霍尔木兹海峡，而且在其他水道也是如此。路透社写道：“霍尔木兹海峡的关闭迫使亚洲政策制定者面临其他海上咽喉要道的安全问题。” 马六甲海峡尤其令人担忧。这是东亚、中东和欧洲之间最重要的航线，约占国际海运贸易的 22%。 但除了海盗和地区冲突之外，还有其他问题值得关注。去年 11 月，战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 对这种新危险发出了警告。 该智库援引红海胡塞民兵的袭击表示，即使是非国家行为者现在也有能力严重扰乱全球贸易流动。许多航运公司现在避免经过苏伊士运河，而是采取绕好望角更长的路线，这对供应链和价格产生了重大影响。 奥地利前陆军上校、奥地利欧洲与安全政策研究所 (AIES) 高级顾问、政治学家尼古拉斯·肖利克 (Nikolaus Scholik) 认为，这些都是地缘政治力量平衡发生根本变化的迹象。 他告诉德国之声：“我们今天正在经历一些发展的后果，个别国家认为他们可以合法地控制具有重要战略意义的海上海峡。”他补充说，如果霍尔木兹、马六甲或台湾等海峡成为地缘政治影响力的杠杆，那将尤其危险。 德国国际与安全事务研究所 (SWP) 亚洲分析师克里斯蒂安·沃斯 (Christian Wirth) 对此表示赞同。 “一个海峡是否特别脆弱主要取决于三个因素：运输协议……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing this week knowing that Xi holds all the cards | Simon Tisdall
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普本周抵达北京，深知习近平掌握所有筹码 | 西蒙·蒂斯代尔

summary.en: The US president is reportedly seeking China's assistance to influence Iran and resolve current diplomatic challenges. This reliance on China comes with a potentially significant cost, including implications for Taiwan.
summary.zh: 据报道，美国总统正在寻求中国的帮助，以影响伊朗并解决当前的国际外交困境。这种对中国的依赖可能带来高昂的代价，包括对台湾的影响。

body.en: The US president will be counting on China to influence Iran and help him out of his latest mess. But the price may be high – including for Taiwan Like an out-of-control wrecking ball, swinging wildly back and forth, Donald Trump smashes up the international order without much thought for the consequences. Lacking coherent strategies, workable plans or consistent aims, he power-trips erratically from one fragile region, tense warzone and complex geopolitical situation to another, leaving misery, confusion and rubble in his wake. Typically, he claims a bogus victory, demands that others repair the damage and pick up the tab, then looks around for something new to break. The president will bulldoze into another international minefield this week – the fraught standoff between China and Taiwan – when he travels to Beijing for a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping. After a string of humiliating policy implosions over Ukraine, Gaza, Nato, Greenland, and now Iran and Lebanon, needy Trump craves a diplomatic success to flaunt at home. But his hopes of vote-winning trade pacts are overshadowed by his latest war of choice. He needs Xi’s promise not to arm Iran if all-out fighting resumes – and Xi’s help keeping the strait of Hormuz open as part of a mooted framework peace deal. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国总统将指望中国影响伊朗并帮助他摆脱最近的困境。但代价可能很高——包括台湾。唐纳德·特朗普就像一个失控的破坏球，疯狂地来回摆动，粉碎了国际秩序，没有考虑到后果。由于缺乏连贯的战略、可行的计划或一致的目标，他的权力不稳定地从一个脆弱地区、紧张战区和复杂的地缘政治局势转移到另一个地区，留下痛苦、混乱和瓦砾。通常，他会声称取得了虚假的胜利，要求其他人修复损坏并承担责任，然后四处寻找新的东西来打破。本周，总统将前往北京与国家主席习近平举行为期两天的峰会，届时他将陷入另一个国际雷区——中国与台湾之间的紧张对峙。在乌克兰、加沙、北约、格陵兰岛，以及现在的伊朗和黎巴嫩等问题上一系列令人羞辱的政策崩溃之后，贫困的特朗普渴望在国内取得外交成功。但他赢得选票的贸易协定的希望被他最近选择的战争所掩盖。他需要习近平承诺，如果全面战争重新爆发，不会武装伊朗 — — 并需要习近平帮助保持霍尔木兹海峡开放，作为拟议框架和平协议的一部分。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In moments of complex international diplomacy, leaders face immense pressure to navigate difficult situations where the stakes are high. When a leader finds themselves in a 'mess' and reliant on others, the need for profound wisdom becomes paramount. James 1:5 reminds us that if anyone lacks wisdom, they should ask God, who gives generously, offering...
reflection.zh: 在复杂的国际外交时刻，领导人面临巨大压力，必须驾驭高风险的困境。当一位领导人发现自己陷入“困境”并依赖他人时，对深刻智慧的需求变得至关重要。雅各书1:5提醒我们，如果有人缺乏智慧，就当向神祈求，神必厚赐于众人，不加责备，提供超越人类策略的指引。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope?
title.zh: 德黑兰、台湾、贸易……特朗普在中美峰会钢丝上将面临哪些危险？

summary.en: The US leader is set to meet with his Chinese counterpart in Beijing for highly anticipated talks. He enters these discussions from a vulnerable position, hoping to secure economic benefits despite a turbulent global environment.
summary.zh: 美国领导人即将前往北京与中国领导人举行备受期待的会谈。他在一个脆弱的立场上进入这些讨论，希望在全球动荡的背景下取得经济上的胜利。

body.en: US leader enters talks with superpower rival from vulnerable position, but will be hoping for economic wins amid turbulent backdrop If all goes to plan over the next few days – and that is a big if – Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a highly anticipated summit with Xi Jinping , China’s leader. The trip will mark the first time a US president has visited China in nearly a decade. The last visit was also made by Trump , during his first term, in 2017. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国领导人处于弱势地位与超级大国竞争对手进行谈判，但希望在动荡的背景下取得经济胜利如果未来几天一切按计划进行 — — 这是一个很大的假设 — — 唐纳德·特朗普将于周三抵达北京，与中国领导人习近平举行备受期待的峰会。此行将是美国总统近十年来首次访华。上次访问也是特朗普在 2017 年第一任期期间进行的。继续阅读...

reflection.en: High-stakes summits between global powers often involve navigating complex challenges and inherent tensions. Romans 12:18 reminds us of the ongoing call to pursue peace, even when circumstances are difficult and outcomes uncertain. It encourages leaders and nations alike to strive for peaceful coexistence, as far as it depends on them.
reflection.zh: 全球大国之间的高峰会晤常常涉及驾驭复杂的挑战和固有的紧张关系。罗马书12:18提醒我们，即使在困难重重、结果不确定的情况下，也要持续追求和平。它鼓励领导人和国家尽其所能，努力实现和平共处。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law on China spies in UK: ‘We’re not surprised’
title.zh: 香港异议人士罗冠聪谈中国在英国的间谍活动：“我们不感到惊讶”

summary.en: Nathan Law, an exiled Hong Kong protest leader, expressed no surprise at the conviction of two men for spying in the UK, which raises concerns about access to sensitive information. Law himself lives with a £100,000 bounty from Chinese authorities.
summary.zh: 流亡的香港抗议领袖罗冠聪对两名男子在英国被判间谍罪表示不意外，这引发了对敏感信息获取方式的严重担忧。罗冠聪本人也面临中国当局悬赏的10万英镑。

body.en: Law says conviction of two men for spying raises serious concerns about how they accessed sensitive information Nathan Law, an exiled leader of the Hong Kong student protest who lives with a £100,000 bounty on his head from the Chinese authorities, was not surprised to discover a spy ring had photographed him entering the Oxford Union for an evening debate in November 2023. The conviction at the Old Bailey of Chi Leung “Peter” Wai, 38, and Chung Biu “Bill” Yuen, 65, for assisting a foreign intelligence service, was a sobering first – no Chinese spies had been convicted in British criminal history before Thursday – but the details that came out in the nine-week trial mainly served to confirm his suspicions. Continue reading...
body.zh: 罗表示，两名男子因间谍罪被定罪，引发了人们对他们如何获取敏感信息的严重担忧。香港学生抗议活动的流亡领袖罗冠聪 (Nathan Law) 生活在中国当局悬赏 10 万英镑的悬赏金中。当他发现间谍团伙拍到他在 2023 年 11 月进入牛津大学联盟参加晚间辩论时，他并不感到惊讶。老贝利法院对 38 岁的 Chi Leung “Peter” Wai 和 Chung Biu “Bill” Yuen 进行了定罪， 65 号协助外国情报部门的指控是一个发人深省的第一次——周四之前，英国犯罪史上还没有中国间谍被定罪——但在为期九周的审判中公布的细节主要证实了他的怀疑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of foreign espionage against dissidents reminds us of the vulnerability of those who speak out against powerful regimes. Proverbs 28:15 describes how a wicked ruler can be like a roaring lion or a charging bear over a helpless people, extending their reach to suppress dissent. In such times, we pray for courage for the persecuted and for justice to...
reflection.zh: 针对异议人士的外国间谍活动提醒我们，那些敢于对抗强大政权的人是多么脆弱。箴言28:15描述了邪恶的统治者如何像咆哮的狮子或冲锋的熊一样对待无助的人民，伸出他们的手压制异议。在这样的时刻，我们为受迫害者祈求勇气，并祈求公义得以伸张。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Former China defence ministers convicted of corruption in latest purge of military leaders
title.zh: 中国前国防部长因腐败被定罪，军事领导层最新一轮清洗

summary.en: Two former Chinese defence ministers, Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe, have been sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve after being convicted of bribery. These are among the most severe sentences in a years-long purge of military leaders.
summary.zh: 中国前国防部长李尚福和魏凤和因受贿罪被判处死刑，缓期两年执行。这是多年来对军事领导人进行清洗中最为严厉的判决之一。

body.en: Ex-defence ministers, Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe both sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, among the most severe sentences in a years-long purge Two former Chinese defence ministers were given suspended death sentences for bribery on Thursday, after being convicted by China’s military court, in some of the most severe punishments to be handed down in a years-long purge of the military. Chinese state media Xinhua announced on Thursday that Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe were both sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, meaning that their sentences will probably be commuted to life imprisonment if Li and Wei demonstrate good behaviour. Continue reading...
body.zh: 前国防部长李尚福和魏凤和双双被判处死刑，缓期两年执行，这是长达一年的整肃行动中最严厉的判决之一。周四，两名前中国国防部长因受贿罪被中国军事法院定罪，被判处死刑缓期执行，这是多年来军队整肃行动中最严厉的一些处罚。中国官方媒体新华社周四宣布，李尚福和魏凤和双双被判处死刑，缓期两年执行，这意味着如果李尚福和魏凤和表现良好，他们的刑期可能会被减为无期徒刑。继续阅读...

This serves as a sober reminder that the pursuit of wealth above all else often results in profound personal and public grief.
reflection.zh: 前国防部长因受贿被定罪，凸显了贪婪的破坏力，即使身居高位者也可能因此面临严峻后果。这提醒我们，将财富置于一切之上，往往会带来深刻的个人和公共悲痛。

title.zh: 英国历史上首次有两人因替中国从事间谍活动而被判有罪

Chi Leung “Peter” Wai, 38, and Chung Biu Yuen, 65, also known as Bill, were found guilty at the Old Bailey of assisting a foreign intelligence service, making them the first people in British history to be convicted of spying for China. body.zh: 池良伟和钟标源因在“影子警务”行动中监视异见人士而被定罪 英国边境部队一名官员和驻伦敦的香港贸易官员被判犯有为中国从事间谍活动并通过“影子警务”行动监视异见人士的罪名。 38 岁的 Chi Leung “Peter” Wai 和 65 岁的 Chung Biu Yuen（又名 Bill）在老贝利被判犯有协助外国情报机构罪，这使他们成为英国历史上第一批因为中国从事间谍活动而被定罪的人。继续阅读...

Jeremiah 22:3 reminds those in authority of their divine mandate to act justly, rescue the oppressed, and do no wrong to the vulnerable, including foreigners. This principle underscores the need for...

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW
title.zh: 香港民主派出版人黎智英获德国之声表彰

summary.en: Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent nearly 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW has awarded Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award.

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

Sebastien Lai, Jimmy Lai's son and a longtime advocate for his release, told DW that "people who fight for freedom, people who fight for the freedom of others are never alone." And it's meaningful at a time when "a lot of media in Hong Kong now are self-censoring."

"I think if he knew about it [the award], he'd be very happy," Sebastien Lai said.             

DW Director General Barbara Massing said that with the award, DW is honoring Jimmy Lai's "indispensable dedication to democratic values."

summary.en: For some men, a lack of emotional resources means profound struggle and suicidal ideation can follow breakups.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
When Tim Hewson's marriage ended, he realised he lacked strong male connections to turn to. Source: SBS / Jack Giam

Tim Hewson vividly remembers the moment he realised the impact of the breakdown of his long-term marriage.

"I started scrolling through my mobile phone thinking, 'Who can I reach out to? Who can I call?'" the 52-year-old told The Feed.

"I realised there wasn't a single bloke in my life that I could really open up to. That's quite a lonely experience."

"I looked in the mirror and the guy staring back at me was someone I never thought I'd become. I was in my early 40s, separated and in the fast lane to divorce. And while I was trying to work out what my life looked like, my thoughts were spiralling out of control."

One in four people who go through a relationship breakdown experience loneliness, according to a 2024 Relationships Australia report, which surveyed about 3,000 people.

But men who experienced a breakup are 82 per cent more likely to report suicidal ideation relative to men without a recent breakup experience, according to a long-term Australian study published in the Journal of Affective Disorders last year that surveyed over 16,000 men and analysed their experiences a year after separation.

One of the authors, Michael Wilson, a research fellow with the Movember Institute, told The Feed some of these negative mental health outcomes were reported by men who had not previously experienced poor mental health.

"Separated men relative to their married counterparts are at up to five times greater risk of suicide," Wilson told The Feed.

While Tim didn't experience suicidal ideation, he said the breakup took a major toll on his mental health.

"Relationship breakdowns are challenging enough, but breaking up families can be even harder — you're now alone," Tim said.

"With isolation and loneliness comes anxiety, depression, and that can lead to a sense of helplessness and hopelessness."

Wilson said many men rely heavily on their partner as their main source of emotional support, which can make breakups particularly difficult.

"The one person through which you typically cope with really intense, stressful experiences is the one person that you now don't necessarily have access to," he said.

But how men navigate distress — shaped by ideas of masculinity and a lack of social and emotional support — may also explain why many men struggle so profoundly after breakups.

For men, romantic relationships can often be the only avenue where vulnerability and emotions feel safe, according to Wilson.

"A lot of guys [in the research] talk about how their partner is the only one that truly knows them," Wilson said.
